sceneFrame.tactical: Ossuary alcoves (4' high, 8' deep) every 10' on both sides.

dressing.text: Bones arranged into lines or clusters.

segments.footingImpact: The stones are broken or dislodged, counting as light rubble; this increases the DC of Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks by 2.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.side: 10' x 10' secret room hidden behind the dead end.
segments.description: Graves and crypts overflow; the dead rise confused or malevolent, filling streets and buildings.
segments.transition: 1: The undead target the living indiscriminately; flight is safer than fight. 2: A necromancer drives the dead toward specific locations or people. 3: The party discovers the rising serves a deeper purpose. 4: Holy ground or running water offers temporary refuge but not escape.

encounter.tactic: Mob Mentality: Civilians or rioters surge forward in mass. They chain the Help action and scatter if their apparent leader falls first.
encounter.text: The Crowd (Corrupt Guard): 2d6+2 Low CR — Mob Mentality: Civilians or rioters surge forward in mass. They chain the Help action and scatter if their apparent leader falls first.

sceneFrame.tactical: Sitting areas (four 10' x 8' alcoves); central statue pedestal.

dressing.text: Mud clumps under a ledge; something nested there.

segments.footingImpact: 2 feet of murky, stagnant water. Counts as _Difficult Terrain_ and grants improved cover to Small creatures.

magic.name: Wand of Conducting
magic.desc: On a gesture, produces a quiet orchestral accompaniment to your actions. No mechanical benefit.

segments.label: Event Scene
segments.side: 10' x 10' reinforced containment cell.
segments.description: A moment where all factions, powers, timelines, and possibilities gather in one space; what happens here echoes across realities.
segments.transition: 1: The party sees multiple versions of themselves and must choose one. 2: The event reshapes the city's entire future in minutes. 3: The party gains or loses knowledge that changes their understanding of reality. 4: This moment is the true end or true beginning of the entire story.

encounter.text: Alchemical/Magical: Illusionary Wall / Floor: A magical prank hides a brick wall or open sewer grate. DC 15 Investigation to discern. Failure means walking face-first into brick or falling 10 feet.

sceneFrame.tactical: 15' drop; 2' high balustrade (no cover, ornamental).

dressing.text: Damp streak down a wall with mineral bloom.

segments.footingImpact: Discarded junk. Counts as _Difficult Terrain_ and increases the DC of Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks by 2.

magic.name: Wand of Pyrotechnics
magic.desc: 7 charges (dawn). Expend 1 charge to produce a harmless burst of colored sparks and pops in a 5-ft area.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.side: 10' x 10' enclosed trapdoor housing.
segments.description: Reality becomes unreliable; physics fails, impossible geometry manifests, and minds break under the weight of wrongness.
segments.transition: 1: The party's sanity is tested; failures result in erratic behavior. 2: The city reshapes itself into nightmare geometry while they traverse it. 3: Others succumb, becoming hazards themselves through their delusion. 4: The cascade originates from something intelligent watching and laughing.

encounter.text: A building is actively collapsing— stone and timber falling into the street, people screaming (rescue workers are forming a line but civilians are still trapped inside)

dressing.text: Damp streak down a wall with mineral bloom.

segments.footingImpact: Collapsed masonry. _Difficult Terrain_. Increases the DC of Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks by 5, and Stealth checks by 2.

magic.name: Bag of Holding
magic.desc: Interior holds 500 lbs / 64 cubic ft; always weighs 15 lbs. Placing a bag inside another destroys both.

segments.label: Breaking Point

finale.revelation: The culprit was hired by someone above them — and that person was hired by someone else; the chain goes higher than the party can currently reach.
finale.exitState: Someone else claims the victory — a local noble, the city guard, a merchant consortium. Your name fades while others grow fat on the credit. The district celebrates the wrong heroes.

sceneFrame.tactical: 25' drop; water channel on inside (narrow, DC 10 to balance).

boss.archetype: Lich pretending to be living noble (undead hidden beneath perfection; unmasking changes fight entirely)

finale.tacticalSetup: Merchant wagon formation — three-four large wagons in defensive circle, wooden sides (half cover), wheels and undercarriage (hazard to crawl under), drivers can crack whips as improvised weapons, mobile if someone takes reins

magic.name: Trident of Fish Command
magic.desc: This magic weapon has 3 charges, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. _(Weapon (Trident), attunement; SRD p.249)_

telegraphs.text: Word on the street: Corrupt Guard holds this ground.

pressureClock.note: Heat is the default — you're already Burning (Heat 3).

segments.sensory: Burnt hair — biological, brief, and recent enough to suggest something nearby was struck by fire.

object.name: Curtain/tapestry
object.flavor: Backing is stiff; hides a recess.

dressing.text: Small clay oil flask, cork swollen tight.

secret.desc: Loose stone / floorboard stash. Trifle + clue fragment (scrap, token, wax seal, chalk mark).

encounter.text: The Staggered Mob (Spider Nest): 2d4 Low CR — Reinforcements: Half the group is present. The others arrive Round 2 through a second entrance, a hidden passage, or from the room behind the party.

valuable.name: A polished river-stone with a hole worn through
valuable.note: A hag-stone. Fishermen pay for the superstition, not the rock.

state.desc: Applies to portcullises, stone slabs, and any door with a mechanical component. Roll 1d2: 1 = stuck open, 2 = stuck closed.

type.desc: A bookcase, weapon rack, or mounted statue rotates on a hidden pivot to reveal a passage; DC to detect the mechanism.

state.name: Spiked Shut
state.desc: Iron spikes driven through the frame from this side; someone didn't want it opened. Requires force and time to clear.

type.name: Chain or Bead Curtain
type.desc: Hanging chains or pierced metal discs; no barrier to movement but audible when passed through.

state.name: Barred From The Far Side
state.desc: Barred from the other side; cannot be opened from this approach without forcing, cutting through, or finding another route.

segments.side: 20' x 20' attached square antechamber; eight stone pilasters built into the curved walls.
segments.scene: Your shadow falls in the wrong direction for a moment, then corrects.
segments.lightFlavor: Dust only exists *inside* the beam—elsewhere it vanishes.
segments.sensory: You smell smoke that isn't there, and the temperature feels a few degrees too warm.

object.name: Sliding grate
object.flavor: Tracks are greased—recently moved.

feature.name: Candelabra
feature.flavor: Blackened tallow clings to its branches.
feature.dims: 3' diameter, 6' high — Minimal cover; knocked over: DC 11 Dex or Prone

dressing.text: Small valve wheel seized halfway open.

secret.desc: Secret encounter space. Prisoner, spy, scavenger, lone monster, or sentry posted in a hidden nook.

encounter.content: The location of whoever is giving orders to the dungeon's current occupants

valuable.name: A folded chart of tide tables, this coastline
valuable.note: Dry reading. A harbormaster would pay for the accuracy.

type.name: Stone Door, Barred
type.desc: Standard stone slab with an iron bar socket cut into the frame on one side. *Bar may or may not be present — see state roll.*

state.name: Locked — Key Elsewhere
state.desc: Locked; key is in a different section of the dungeon, or held by the boss.

type.name: Open Archway, Wide
type.desc: No door. 12' wide dressed stone arch, 10' high. *Ruin skin: partially collapsed, one keystone missing.*

type.name: Single Iron Door

state.name: Barred From The Far Side

segments.side: 5' x 10' triangular dead-end pocket at the outer corner; iron spike driven into the wall.
segments.scene: The room is entirely clean — not scrubbed, just never dirtied. It was sealed before anything could accumulate.
segments.lightFlavor: The dark has gradients—barely—like deep water.
segments.sensory: Something has been feeding here. The smell is dry and organic, like a predator's den between meals.

object.name: Note scrap
object.flavor: Just a name and a number—ominous.

feature.name: Collapsed Bridge
feature.flavor: One end holds, the other sags at a sharp angle.
feature.dims: 15' span at 30° decline — DC 12 Acrobatics to cross; DC 14 at full speed

dressing.text: Scored door with many shallow blade nicks.

secret.desc: Hollow feature compartment. Inside statue, pillar, brazier base, cracked urn (requires interaction).
secret.skills: Perception / Nature / Medicine (rot, ozone, incense, spores)

encounter.text: Draft of Fresh Air — A faint breeze suggests a crack or route. Route hint: next secret route reveal gets advantage to find (Perception/Investigation).

valuable.name: A small block of pressed tea
valuable.note: Compressed hard as brick, ages well, worth more the older it gets.

type.name: Cave Mouth, Submerged
type.desc: Opening partially or fully below water level; requires swimming or draining to use. *Fortress skin: treat as a sluice gate.*

state.name: Roll Twice
state.desc: Roll twice on this table; both conditions apply simultaneously. (e.g., Barred from the far side AND trapped.)

type.name: Main: Double Iron / Secondary: Floor Hatch
type.desc: Double iron main doors plus a 2' x 2' floor hatch 5' away leading to a crawl passage below.

state.name: Trapped — Visible
state.desc: A trap element is detectable on approach: tripwire across the threshold, pressure plate, or obvious trigger mechanism. Can be disarmed.

type.name: Cave Mouth, Stalactite Fringe
type.desc: Wide irregular cave opening (8' x 6'); stalactites reduce effective clearance to 5'.

state.name: Barred From This Side
state.desc: Heavy bar across the inside face; lifted freely from this side, impossible from the other without forcing or a workaround.

type.desc: Iron portcullis; mechanism frozen with age — roll 1d2: 1 = stuck open, 2 = stuck closed; ignores state roll.

state.name: Trapped — Concealed
state.desc: A hidden trap; DC to detect before triggering. Effect may be alarm, damage, gas, or mechanical (portcullis drop, pit).

segments.scene: A candle was snuffed very recently. The smoke still rises in a thin column.
segments.lightFlavor: Green light concentrates near cracks and vents.
segments.sensory: The place is humid, and you hear slow dripping that never quite matches its echo.

object.name: Lens/prism
object.flavor: Splits light into odd slivers.

feature.name: Support Pillars
feature.flavor: A chipped pillar bears faded chisel marks.
feature.dims: 5'×5' base, 18' high — Total cover; DC 12 Arcana reads the mason's ward marks

dressing.text: Rusted manacles, one link freshly broken.

secret.desc: Major route revelation. Shortcut to approach/finale region, escape tunnel, hidden stair to another depth (optional).

type.desc: Thick fabric or hide hanging, floor to ceiling; no mechanical door, but announces movement when disturbed. *Noble skin: rich tapestry. Cave skin: matted moss or hide.*

state.name: Chained and Padlocked
state.desc: A chain loops through the handle and a ring in the wall; padlock holds it. Chain can be broken or lock picked.

segments.side: 15' x 15' open shaft in the center dropping 40 ft; iron rungs set into one wall of the shaft; 5' walkway around the shaft perimeter.
segments.scene: Someone lived in this room for a long time. You can see it in the worn stone, the hook in the wall, the small space they arranged for themselves.
segments.lightFlavor: The beam trembles slightly with every breath.
segments.sensory: A low, pervasive sweetness of old fungus — not the sharp stink of rot, just wrong and faintly cloying.

object.name: Salt crust
object.flavor: Crumbles into powder that clings to boots.

feature.name: Iron Portcullis
feature.flavor: Rusted teeth half-sunk into the stone floor.

dressing.text: Offering dish with dried petals/ashes.

secret.desc: Hollow feature compartment. Inside statue, pillar, brazier base, cracked urn (requires interaction).

type.name: Trust the room
type.desc: The puzzle lies to you. The obvious solution is the trap; the safe-looking path is the death. Read what the room *wants* you to do, then don't.

mechanism.setup: A series of plates, levers, or tiles wired to one door.
mechanism.locked: One is already depressed and glowing faintly — a started sequence.
mechanism.failConsequence: The whole sequence resets to zero with an audible *thunk*.

solutionPath.path: Answer the living warden on its terms — soothe, feed, name, or honestly bargain with it instead of fighting.
solutionPath.skillDc: Cha (Persuasion/Insight) or a fitting offering; DC 16.

failsafe.name: Pay-a-cost bypass
failsafe.desc: The room accepts *defeat* as an answer: say "I can't" aloud and mean it, and it opens out of something like pity — but it remembers you bent, and the place is colder to you after.

DC 14 Int (Arcana) to identify the area before stepping in. Destroying the artifact (AC 13, 10 HP) ends the effect.

magic.name: Rope of Mending
magic.desc: A 10-foot rope that can reassemble itself when commanded, once per short rest.

valuable.name: A folded square of good wool cloth
valuable.note: Dyed a deep blue that took real money to make.

mechanism.locked: It's visibly *moving* — slow, patient, watching back.
mechanism.failConsequence: It scrambles further the harder you stare; brute scrutiny makes it worse.

segments.description: A narrow alley choked by market stalls becomes a kill zone as enemies close from both ends, collapsing escape routes.
segments.transition: 1: One exit floods with enemy reinforcements; the party chooses fight or a dangerous rooftop sprint. 2: A stall collapses, blocking retreat but creating a temporary barrier against pursuers. 3: A faction hired the ambushers—the party stumbles onto a larger conspiracy. 4: Innocents caught in the crossfire force a moral choice that slows the party's movement.

encounter.text: Loud Gravel Roof — DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) to cross without crunching, or DC 13 Wisdom (Nature) to find mossy patches.

sceneFrame.tactical: Reinforced door midway; 5' x 5' inspection cell to side.

dressing.text: Chamber pot behind a board screen.

segments.footingImpact: A localized skylight to the dungeon below.

valuable.name: A compass that points toward the nearest open grave
valuable.note: Reliable. Nobody's asked it to stop.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.side: 5' x 10' attached privy/closet.
segments.description: A reservoir barrier cracks and ruptures; water floods the lower city with frightening speed, drowning everything it touches.
segments.transition: 1: The party must reach high ground or be swept away. 2: Innocents are trapped in flooded districts; rescue attempts cost precious movement. 3: The flood reveals sunken ruins and hidden passages. 4: The catastrophe reshapes the city's geography and factions' power bases.

encounter.tactic: Divide & Conquer: The pair splits the party by forcing them into separate alleys, rooms, or buildings, then engages each group separately.
encounter.text: The Elite Pair (Corrupt Guard): 2 Mid-High CR — Divide & Conquer: The pair splits the party by forcing them into separate alleys, rooms, or buildings, then engages each group separately.

sceneFrame.tactical: 5' x 25' ornamental railing dividing roadway.

dressing.text: Rotting banner with a faint symbol.

segments.footingImpact: Treated as a 20-foot-deep pit trap that cannot be reset. Falling deals 2d6 Bludgeoning damage and knocks the target Prone.

valuable.name: A carved antler comb
valuable.note: A few teeth broken. Still combs out a knot.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.side: 10' x 20' attached stables.
segments.description: A warehouse's top floor ignites; smoke rolls into adjacent streets and the conflagration spreads with each passing round.
segments.transition: 1: The fire cuts off a planned escape route—party must find a new path. 2: Fleeing refugees panic and block the party's advance. 3: A building next door collapses, trapping innocents the party must rescue or abandon. 4: The chaos attracts rival faction members scrambling to salvage goods.

encounter.text: Carved History — Plaques, dates, or names etched into stone or wood reveal the area's past. Gain a piece of historical lore or advantage on one Intelligence check related to the district's history.

dressing.text: Narrow passage with scrape marks at shoulder height.

atmo.text: a sudden metallic clang followed by muttering

segments.footingImpact: Wet, clinging muck. Counts as _Difficult Terrain_. Any creature knocked Prone in the mud must use all of its movement (instead of half) to stand up.

segments.label: Hub
segments.side: 10' x 20' attached hallway.
segments.description: A flophouse where guests share feverish prophetic dreams; the landlord claims the building sits on a ley line and charges extra for the visions
segments.transition: 1: Through the cellar where the ley line hums to underground passages 2: Out the common room to the boulevard 3: Via the fire escape to the rooftop and its strange antenna 4: Down through the dreaming ward to a sleepwalker's tunnel 5: Through a crack in the wall that shouldn't lead anywhere but does 6: Across the courtyard where reality feels slightly thin

encounter.text: Street Performer — DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) to realize they are a pickpocket or DC 13 Dexterity (Stealth) to blend in.

sceneFrame.tactical: Guard station (8' x 8'); registry desk blocks center.

dressing.text: Cloth tag tied to a hook with initials.

segments.footingImpact: A collapsed wall blocking the path. Counts as _Difficult Terrain_.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.side: 10' wide open balcony wrapping the upper perimeter.
segments.description: A location begins devouring reality around it; matter, people, and light vanish into nothing; the void expands inexorably.
segments.transition: 1: The party must race away from the expanding edge. 2: Those at the void's margin experience existence breaking down. 3: The void's source is a person, artifact, or ritual that must be stopped. 4: The void leaves survivors changed or partially unmade.

encounter.tactic: Divide & Conquer: The pair splits the party by forcing them into separate alleys, rooms, or buildings, then engages each group separately.
encounter.text: The Elite Pair (Corrupt Guard): 2 Mid-High CR — Divide & Conquer: The pair splits the party by forcing them into separate alleys, rooms, or buildings, then engages each group separately.

sceneFrame.tactical: Four covered walks (8' deep); central garden well (6' diameter).

dressing.text: Snapped chain with the broken link missing.

segments.footingImpact: A cluster of young mimics imitating a crosswalk. Triggers a multi-target grapple ambush.

backgroundEvent.text: The Animated Statue: A stone statue of a past local ruler suddenly animates and begins shouting curses at passersby.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.side: Fully ruined roof, 10' x 20' intact covered side-area.
segments.description: A crowd ignited by rumor, preaching, or panic swells and turns violent, surging toward the party's position.
segments.transition: 1: The mob's direction changes; they flow toward a new target the party must defend or exploit. 2: Faction agitators within the crowd drive it deeper into dangerous territory, dragging the party along. 3: The party is separated in the press; rejoining costs time or a detour through unstable areas. 4: The mob's fury draws official response—armed militia or summoned guards arrive to disperse them.

encounter.text: Urban Terrain: Deep Mud / Offal: A section of unpaved slum is flooded with muck. Treat as Difficult Terrain. A DC 11 Constitution save is required to avoid retching (Disadvantage on next attack/check).

sceneFrame.tactical: Ossuary alcoves (4' high, 8' deep) every 10' on both sides.

dressing.text: Bones arranged into lines or clusters.

segments.footingImpact: The stones are broken or dislodged, counting as light rubble; this increases the DC of Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks by 2.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.side: 10' x 10' secret room hidden behind the dead end.
segments.description: Graves and crypts overflow; the dead rise confused or malevolent, filling streets and buildings.
segments.transition: 1: The undead target the living indiscriminately; flight is safer than fight. 2: A necromancer drives the dead toward specific locations or people. 3: The party discovers the rising serves a deeper purpose. 4: Holy ground or running water offers temporary refuge but not escape.

encounter.tactic: Mob Mentality: Civilians or rioters surge forward in mass. They chain the Help action and scatter if their apparent leader falls first.
encounter.text: The Crowd (Corrupt Guard): 2d6+2 Low CR — Mob Mentality: Civilians or rioters surge forward in mass. They chain the Help action and scatter if their apparent leader falls first.

sceneFrame.tactical: Sitting areas (four 10' x 8' alcoves); central statue pedestal.

dressing.text: Mud clumps under a ledge; something nested there.

segments.footingImpact: 2 feet of murky, stagnant water. Counts as _Difficult Terrain_ and grants improved cover to Small creatures.

magic.name: Wand of Conducting
magic.desc: On a gesture, produces a quiet orchestral accompaniment to your actions. No mechanical benefit.

segments.label: Event Scene
segments.side: 10' x 10' reinforced containment cell.
segments.description: A moment where all factions, powers, timelines, and possibilities gather in one space; what happens here echoes across realities.
segments.transition: 1: The party sees multiple versions of themselves and must choose one. 2: The event reshapes the city's entire future in minutes. 3: The party gains or loses knowledge that changes their understanding of reality. 4: This moment is the true end or true beginning of the entire story.

encounter.text: Alchemical/Magical: Illusionary Wall / Floor: A magical prank hides a brick wall or open sewer grate. DC 15 Investigation to discern. Failure means walking face-first into brick or falling 10 feet.

sceneFrame.tactical: 15' drop; 2' high balustrade (no cover, ornamental).

dressing.text: Damp streak down a wall with mineral bloom.

segments.footingImpact: Discarded junk. Counts as _Difficult Terrain_ and increases the DC of Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks by 2.

magic.name: Wand of Pyrotechnics
magic.desc: 7 charges (dawn). Expend 1 charge to produce a harmless burst of colored sparks and pops in a 5-ft area.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.side: 10' x 10' enclosed trapdoor housing.
segments.description: Reality becomes unreliable; physics fails, impossible geometry manifests, and minds break under the weight of wrongness.
segments.transition: 1: The party's sanity is tested; failures result in erratic behavior. 2: The city reshapes itself into nightmare geometry while they traverse it. 3: Others succumb, becoming hazards themselves through their delusion. 4: The cascade originates from something intelligent watching and laughing.

encounter.text: A building is actively collapsing— stone and timber falling into the street, people screaming (rescue workers are forming a line but civilians are still trapped inside)

dressing.text: Damp streak down a wall with mineral bloom.

segments.footingImpact: Collapsed masonry. _Difficult Terrain_. Increases the DC of Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks by 5, and Stealth checks by 2.

magic.name: Bag of Holding
magic.desc: Interior holds 500 lbs / 64 cubic ft; always weighs 15 lbs. Placing a bag inside another destroys both.

segments.label: Breaking Point
segments.side: 20' x 20' central pit; 10' x 10' control room attached.

finale.revelation: The culprit was hired by someone above them — and that person was hired by someone else; the chain goes higher than the party can currently reach.
finale.exitState: Someone else claims the victory — a local noble, the city guard, a merchant consortium. Your name fades while others grow fat on the credit. The district celebrates the wrong heroes.

sceneFrame.tactical: 25' drop; water channel on inside (narrow, DC 10 to balance).

boss.archetype: Lich pretending to be living noble (undead hidden beneath perfection; unmasking changes fight entirely)

finale.tacticalSetup: Merchant wagon formation — three-four large wagons in defensive circle, wooden sides (half cover), wheels and undercarriage (hazard to crawl under), drivers can crack whips as improvised weapons, mobile if someone takes reins

magic.name: Trident of Fish Command
magic.desc: This magic weapon has 3 charges, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. _(Weapon (Trident), attunement; SRD p.249)_

telegraphs.text: Word on the street: Corrupt Guard holds this ground.

pressureClock.note: Heat is the default — you're already Burning (Heat 3).

encounterResolution.objectiveRef: escape the captains with the courier report

encounterResolution.method: failed smoke rescue followed by an exact marker and fire-call
encounterResolution.outcome: failed rescue; collapse marked for responders

encounterResolution.method: perfectly timed runoff crawl beneath the crowd’s sightline
encounterResolution.objectiveRef: escape the mob surge through the drainage arch

macguffin.name: Temporarily Existing Thing
macguffin.desc: Only real for a short time.

complication.name: Recursive Space
complication.desc: Easy to re-enter, hard to exit.

walk.topologyDesc: Multiple overlapping loops with cross-connections. High navigational complexity. Best for mystery or heist dungeons.

threat.scale: 1d4 per room; 1 Mid per 2 rooms; 1 Boss at finale
threat.signs: Fine web strands at face height across corridors; bundled prey in corners; fresh silk construction in progress

setup.originFlavor: Border fortifications built for long campaigns.
setup.skinVisual: Roots lace across the ceiling like veins.
setup.motifDesc: Hands tying cords/prayer knots. Knot pattern can encode a simple clue.
setup.motifModifierDesc: Intact and readable. Advantage on the first check to interpret/find a related secret this dungeon.
setup.restDesc: The rest is violently interrupted by a nearby Threat. No recovery benefits.

skin.text: A faction's spy has already mapped this place. — A detailed, accurate sketch, dropped or hidden, in a hand that belongs to someone with resources and a clear reason to care about this dungeon.

segments.label: Entry

type.name: Wooden Door, Reinforced
type.desc: 3' x 7' plank door banded with iron straps; iron ring handle; noticeably sturdier than standard.

state.name: Open / Standing Ajar
state.desc: No obstruction. Passage is clear and the door's position is visible from the approach.

type.name: Double Stone Slabs
type.desc: Two 3' x 7' stone slabs on heavy iron hinges; bar socket carved directly into the stone frame.

state.name: Open / Standing Ajar
state.desc: No obstruction. Passage is clear and the door's position is visible from the approach.

type.name: Main: Double Wooden / Flanking: Iron Gates
type.desc: Double wooden main doors; two narrow iron-barred alcove gates flank the opening on both sides.

state.name: Locked — No Key
state.desc: Designed to stay shut. Requires picking, forcing, or an alternate route. No key was ever meant to exist here.

segments.side: 5' x 5' recessed niche in each wall, facing each other; arrow-loop slots carved above each niche.
segments.scene: The walls were inscribed with something, then deliberately effaced. The erasure is as careful as the inscription was.
segments.lightFlavor: Fine detail blurs; big shapes dominate.
segments.sensory: Burnt hair — biological, brief, and recent enough to suggest something nearby was struck by fire.

object.name: Curtain/tapestry
object.flavor: Backing is stiff; hides a recess.

feature.name: Sarcophagus
feature.flavor: A carved lid depicts a stern figure.
feature.dims: 7'×3' footprint, 4' high — Half cover; lid 300 lbs (DC 15 Str or two people to open)

dressing.text: Small clay oil flask, cork swollen tight.

secret.desc: Loose stone / floorboard stash. Trifle + clue fragment (scrap, token, wax seal, chalk mark).

encounter.tactic: Reinforcements: Half the group is present. The others arrive Round 2 through a second entrance, a hidden passage, or from the room behind the party.
encounter.text: The Staggered Mob (Spider Nest): 2d4 Low CR — Reinforcements: Half the group is present. The others arrive Round 2 through a second entrance, a hidden passage, or from the room behind the party.

valuable.name: A polished river-stone with a hole worn through
valuable.note: A hag-stone. Fishermen pay for the superstition, not the rock.

type.name: Stone Door, No Handle
type.desc: No external latch or handle visible; opens via push-pressure, counterweight, or hidden trigger.

state.name: Mechanism Jammed
state.desc: Applies to portcullises, stone slabs, and any door with a mechanical component. Roll 1d2: 1 = stuck open, 2 = stuck closed.

type.name: Rotating Fixture
type.desc: A bookcase, weapon rack, or mounted statue rotates on a hidden pivot to reveal a passage; DC to detect the mechanism.

state.name: Spiked Shut
state.desc: Iron spikes driven through the frame from this side; someone didn't want it opened. Requires force and time to clear.

type.name: Chain or Bead Curtain
type.desc: Hanging chains or pierced metal discs; no barrier to movement but audible when passed through.

state.name: Barred From The Far Side
state.desc: Barred from the other side; cannot be opened from this approach without forcing, cutting through, or finding another route.

segments.side: 20' x 20' attached square antechamber; eight stone pilasters built into the curved walls.
segments.scene: Your shadow falls in the wrong direction for a moment, then corrects.
segments.lightFlavor: Dust only exists *inside* the beam—elsewhere it vanishes.
segments.sensory: You smell smoke that isn't there, and the temperature feels a few degrees too warm.

object.name: Sliding grate
object.flavor: Tracks are greased—recently moved.

feature.name: Candelabra
feature.flavor: Blackened tallow clings to its branches.
feature.dims: 3' diameter, 6' high — Minimal cover; knocked over: DC 11 Dex or Prone

dressing.text: Small valve wheel seized halfway open.

secret.desc: Secret encounter space. Prisoner, spy, scavenger, lone monster, or sentry posted in a hidden nook.

encounter.form: Remains so old only the equipment survives — but the equipment is identifiable
encounter.content: The location of whoever is giving orders to the dungeon's current occupants
encounter.text: Remains so old only the equipment survives — but the equipment is identifiable: The location of whoever is giving orders to the dungeon's current occupants

valuable.name: A folded chart of tide tables, this coastline
valuable.note: Dry reading. A harbormaster would pay for the accuracy.

type.name: Stone Door, Barred
type.desc: Standard stone slab with an iron bar socket cut into the frame on one side. *Bar may or may not be present — see state roll.*

state.name: Locked — Key Elsewhere
state.desc: Locked; key is in a different section of the dungeon, or held by the boss.

type.name: Open Archway, Wide
type.desc: No door. 12' wide dressed stone arch, 10' high. *Ruin skin: partially collapsed, one keystone missing.*

state.name: Roll Twice
state.desc: Roll twice on this table; both conditions apply simultaneously. (e.g., Barred from the far side AND trapped.)

type.name: Single Iron Door
type.desc: Heavy 3' x 7' iron door, flat face, iron ring handle; hinges intact and functional.

state.name: Magically Sealed
state.desc: Longer-duration or permanent seal; requires a specific key word, object, or condition to open. Forcing damages the sealing effect.

type.name: Single Iron Door
type.desc: Heavy 3' x 7' iron door, flat face, iron ring handle; hinges intact and functional.

state.name: Barred From The Far Side
state.desc: Barred from the other side; cannot be opened from this approach without forcing, cutting through, or finding another route.

segments.side: 5' x 10' triangular dead-end pocket at the outer corner; iron spike driven into the wall.
segments.scene: The room is entirely clean — not scrubbed, just never dirtied. It was sealed before anything could accumulate.
segments.lightFlavor: The dark has gradients—barely—like deep water.
segments.sensory: Something has been feeding here. The smell is dry and organic, like a predator's den between meals.

object.name: Note scrap
object.flavor: Just a name and a number—ominous.

feature.name: Collapsed Bridge
feature.flavor: One end holds, the other sags at a sharp angle.
feature.dims: 15' span at 30° decline — DC 12 Acrobatics to cross; DC 14 at full speed

dressing.text: Scored door with many shallow blade nicks.

secret.desc: Hollow feature compartment. Inside statue, pillar, brazier base, cracked urn (requires interaction).
secret.skills: Perception / Nature / Medicine (rot, ozone, incense, spores)

encounter.text: Draft of Fresh Air — A faint breeze suggests a crack or route. Route hint: next secret route reveal gets advantage to find (Perception/Investigation).

valuable.name: A small block of pressed tea
valuable.note: Compressed hard as brick, ages well, worth more the older it gets.

type.name: Cave Mouth, Submerged
type.desc: Opening partially or fully below water level; requires swimming or draining to use. *Fortress skin: treat as a sluice gate.*

state.name: Roll Twice
state.desc: Roll twice on this table; both conditions apply simultaneously. (e.g., Barred from the far side AND trapped.)

type.name: Main: Double Iron / Secondary: Floor Hatch
type.desc: Double iron main doors plus a 2' x 2' floor hatch 5' away leading to a crawl passage below.

state.name: Trapped — Visible
state.desc: A trap element is detectable on approach: tripwire across the threshold, pressure plate, or obvious trigger mechanism. Can be disarmed.

type.name: Cave Mouth, Stalactite Fringe
type.desc: Wide irregular cave opening (8' x 6'); stalactites reduce effective clearance to 5'.

state.name: Barred From This Side
state.desc: Heavy bar across the inside face; lifted freely from this side, impossible from the other without forcing or a workaround.

type.name: Portcullis, Rusted
type.desc: Iron portcullis; mechanism frozen with age — roll 1d2: 1 = stuck open, 2 = stuck closed; ignores state roll.

state.name: Trapped — Concealed
state.desc: A hidden trap; DC to detect before triggering. Effect may be alarm, damage, gas, or mechanical (portcullis drop, pit).

segments.side: 15' x 15' central junction room; remains of a collapsed stone signpost at the center.
segments.scene: A candle was snuffed very recently. The smoke still rises in a thin column.
segments.lightFlavor: Green light concentrates near cracks and vents.
segments.sensory: The place is humid, and you hear slow dripping that never quite matches its echo.

object.name: Lens/prism
object.flavor: Splits light into odd slivers.

feature.name: Support Pillars
feature.flavor: A chipped pillar bears faded chisel marks.
feature.dims: 5'×5' base, 18' high — Total cover; DC 12 Arcana reads the mason's ward marks

dressing.text: Rusted manacles, one link freshly broken.

secret.desc: Major route revelation. Shortcut to approach/finale region, escape tunnel, hidden stair to another depth (optional).

encounter.revelation: There is a fixed end point — the dungeon has always been moving toward a specific conclusion, and this room marks how close it is
encounter.art: A single image covering the entire far wall: the dungeon as it will look when it is finished. Some elements match the current state. Others do not exist yet.
encounter.text: Lore: There is a fixed end point — the dungeon has always been moving toward a specific conclusion, and this room marks how close it is

valuable.name: A brass shaving razor in a felt case
valuable.note: Barber's kit, well kept, half-used strop included.

type.name: Iron Door, Knee Hatch
type.desc: Full 3' x 7' iron door plus a separate 18" square iron hatch at knee height, separately latched.

state.name: Closed, Unlocked
state.desc: Closed but opens freely; no key or force required.

type.name: Wooden Door, Reinforced
type.desc: 3' x 7' plank door banded with iron straps; iron ring handle; noticeably sturdier than standard.

state.name: Locked — Key in This Zone
state.desc: Locked; key is carried by a creature or hidden in an object within this dungeon section.

type.name: Heavy Curtain
type.desc: Thick fabric or hide hanging, floor to ceiling; no mechanical door, but announces movement when disturbed. *Noble skin: rich tapestry. Cave skin: matted moss or hide.*

state.name: Chained and Padlocked
state.desc: A chain loops through the handle and a ring in the wall; padlock holds it. Chain can be broken or lock picked.

segments.side: 15' x 15' open shaft in the center dropping 40 ft; iron rungs set into one wall of the shaft; 5' walkway around the shaft perimeter.
segments.scene: Someone lived in this room for a long time. You can see it in the worn stone, the hook in the wall, the small space they arranged for themselves.
segments.lightFlavor: The beam trembles slightly with every breath.
segments.sensory: A low, pervasive sweetness of old fungus — not the sharp stink of rot, just wrong and faintly cloying.

object.name: Salt crust
object.flavor: Crumbles into powder that clings to boots.

feature.name: Iron Portcullis
feature.flavor: Rusted teeth half-sunk into the stone floor.
feature.dims: 10' wide, 10' high — Impassable; Str DC 17 to lift; winch likely nearby

dressing.text: Offering dish with dried petals/ashes.

secret.desc: Hollow feature compartment. Inside statue, pillar, brazier base, cracked urn (requires interaction).

type.name: Trust the room
type.desc: The puzzle lies to you. The obvious solution is the trap; the safe-looking path is the death. Read what the room *wants* you to do, then don't.

mechanism.setup: A series of plates, levers, or tiles wired to one door.
mechanism.locked: One is already depressed and glowing faintly — a started sequence.
mechanism.failConsequence: The whole sequence resets to zero with an audible *thunk*.

solutionPath.path: Answer the living warden on its terms — soothe, feed, name, or honestly bargain with it instead of fighting.
solutionPath.skillDc: Cha (Persuasion/Insight) or a fitting offering; DC 16.

failsafe.name: Pay-a-cost bypass
failsafe.desc: The room accepts *defeat* as an answer: say "I can't" aloud and mean it, and it opens out of something like pity — but it remembers you bent, and the place is colder to you after.

encounter.text: Dead-Magic Pocket: A 20-foot-radius area where magic fails entirely. Spell slots cannot be expended, verbal components don't function, magic items become inert. Caused by a residual artifact at the center. — Mundane Solution: Must be crossed without magic. Concentration spells drop immediately on entry. DC 14 Int (Arcana) to identify the area before stepping in. Destroying the artifact (AC 13, 10 HP) ends the effect.

magic.name: Rope of Mending
magic.desc: A 10-foot rope that can reassemble itself when commanded, once per short rest.

valuable.name: A folded square of good wool cloth
valuable.note: Dyed a deep blue that took real money to make.

segments.label: Branch

type.name: Wooden Postern
type.desc: Small 2' x 6' utility door set beside or independent of a larger opening; iron latch, no lock. *Fortress skin: iron-banded.*

state.name: Locked — Key in This Zone
state.desc: Locked; key is carried by a creature or hidden in an object within this dungeon section.

segments.side: Overlooks the cell fronts below; iron stair or ladder access; desk and key-ring pegs bolted to the rail.
segments.scene: Water has started seeping from somewhere. A thin line appears at the base of the far wall, growing slowly.
segments.lightFlavor: You feel the walls before you see them.
segments.sensory: A static charge hangs in the air — hair stands up, metal warms to the touch, stone hums below hearing.

object.name: Tripwire line
object.flavor: Thin and taut; tied to a nail.

feature.name: Magical Font
feature.flavor: Marble basin filled with glowing liquid.
feature.dims: 5'×5' footprint, 3' high — Half cover; Arcana DC 12 identifies properties

dressing.text: A thick rug rolled and stood against the corner, damp-heavy and sour to the nose.

secret.desc: Hidden compartment with meaning. Clue + usable reward (map scrap, key, antitoxin, scroll, etc.).

encounter.terrain: Difficult terrain — mud/rubble/roots/ice; speed & shoves matter

magic.name: Spell Scroll — 1st Level
magic.desc: Roll d8: 1 Cure Wounds, 2 Shield, 3 Detect Magic, 4 Alarm, 5 Jump, 6 Feather Fall, 7 Sleep, 8 Fog Cloud.

segments.lightFlavor: Bruised purple bands; “stain stops” imply ward lines.
segments.sensory: The floor is slick, and the air carries a green, loamy rot like overturned compost.

object.name: Mud bank
object.flavor: Footprints preserve sharply here.

feature.name: Stone Altar
feature.flavor: Melted wax pools along carved edges.
feature.dims: 5'×3' footprint, 4' high — Half cover; wax record is legible with DC 13 Arcana

dressing.text: Bedroll and blanket, neatly rolled, too neat.

secret.desc: Major route revelation. Shortcut to approach/finale region, escape tunnel, hidden stair to another depth (optional).

type.name: Living lock
type.desc: A creature, bound or sleeping, *is* the door — it must be answered, soothed, fed, or outwitted, not broken.

mechanism.setup: A grid of symbols you must complete or correct.
mechanism.locked: The pattern is 90% laid; the gap is obvious, the *fill* is not.
mechanism.failConsequence: A wrong glyph flares red and goes dark; one strike against you (see Failsafe).

solutionPath.path: Answer the riddle — its wording points to one concrete, in-world thing the player can name or fetch.
solutionPath.skillDc: Player figures it; or History/Arcana hint, DC 15.

failsafe.name: Brute alternative
failsafe.desc: Any sensible off-book idea the player improvises works on a single skill check — honor the cool (§5) and let creativity be the key.

dmlog.text: I stand in the tannery doorway and play a sharp three-note call on my lute, watching who looks toward the storm rather than toward me.

The three notes skip from pane to pane through the fused-glass street. Most faces turn toward you. Two do not: a child crouched beneath an oilskin watches the drain grates, and a one-eyed courier with a lacquered message tube watches the black seam of cloud closing over the sea-caves. At your third note, the courier answers with three taps against the tube—not applause, but recognition. “If that was a warning,” they say, “you are late. If it was a summons, choose who you mean to save.” Wind drives the first cold rain through the tannery door, carrying the low roar of water from somewhere beneath the cobbles.

ruling.understoodAction: Use a conspicuous musical signal to identify people already focused on the approaching storm.
ruling.ruling: Ordinary observation reveals who reacts differently; no roll is needed until Mira tries to influence, deceive, or read concealed intent.
ruling.stakes: The storm is now close enough to begin affecting the street.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 1: player-authored motif reciprocated; open handoff preserved. The courier becomes consequential and is engine-minted through gen[npc].

dmlog.text: ⚙ the world provides — npc rolled
I answer the courier with three taps on the lute's body, then hold out my empty right hand. “Mira Quill. Tell me who needs shelter first—and who profits if they do not find it.”

The courier takes your right hand with rain already shining on their knuckles. “William Sallow.” Their gaze flicks once to your left hand, confirming that you understood the insult you did not give. “The cave-cutters below Low Sluice need the dry galleries. The Crier’s Circle sealed those galleries at midnight for message stores that could survive perfectly well upstairs.” William turns the lacquered tube so you can see its wax seal has been broken and pressed closed again. “Someone altered the evacuation order. I can prove where it was opened. I cannot prove who changed it.” Beneath the street, the water’s roar briefly resolves into something like a long, sleeping breath.

payload.what: The Low Sluice evacuation order was altered after sealing; the Crier's Circle reserved the dry galleries for message stores while cave-cutters remain exposed.

ruling.understoodAction: Respect the local hand taboo and ask the identified courier who is endangered and who benefits.
ruling.ruling: William answers because the gesture establishes basic respect and Mira asks for facts he is already trying to expose.
ruling.stakes: The storm and altered evacuation order create a time-sensitive but still open problem.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 2: direct question receives actionable truth, preserves off-menu freedom, and contacts the engine-minted NPC. Pressure is tied to the rolled storm and faction rather than imposed travel.

dmlog.text: I crouch beside the child and use Minor Illusion to repeat the breathing sound from the drain at the mouth of William's message tube, watching whether he recognizes it. “Before we run to the galleries, tell me whether this storm is the only thing trying to get inside.”

Your copied breath slips into the lacquered tube and comes back thin and metallic. William’s jaw tightens, but the child shakes their head. “Too even,” they whisper. Then the real sound answers from a drain three paces away—one long pull of air against the rain. William says, “The old evacuation route runs beneath Low Sluice. It was bricked shut before I was born.” Your imitation has given you a clean comparison; now you can listen for where the true cadence travels.

ruling.understoodAction: Use Minor Illusion as a controlled sound to compare the strange breathing and read William's recognition.
ruling.ruling: The cantrip creates a valid reference sound. Investigation determines how much Mira can infer from the resulting echoes; William freely confirms the known existence of the old route.

dmlog.text: Your illusion and the hollow tube multiply the echo until every grate seems to breathe. When you end the spell, the real cadence has stopped; you have learned it can react to sound, but not where it traveled.
I stop making noise, light one of my candles, cup it against the rain, and carry the flame low over each drain until it bends toward a draft. “Nothing breathes without moving air.”
(No DM answered. The bridge is running, but a DM session needs to be watching it — start one per docs/DM-BRIDGE.md, ideally on Sonnet for speed. Or use ✦ Copy world for the clipboard hand-off.)

I wedge the lit candle upright in the seam as a draft marker. “William, bring the cave-cutters here instead of downhill.” Then I use my dagger's pommel to work the first translucent peg loose. I do not wait for anyone's permission.

The first peg slides free with a glassy chirp. The grate lifts a finger’s width and exhales hard enough to flatten the candle flame; warm salt air—not rain-cold wind—spills around your boots. William looks from the opening to the families running downhill. “I’ll turn them here,” he says. “If this is a trap, keep it alive until I return.” He sprints into the rain, striking your three-note rhythm on his message tube. The child stays, counting the two remaining pegs aloud while your candle marks the draft.

I leave the last peg seated. “What do I call you, and what have you seen come out of these drains?” I ask the child. While they answer, I press my ear near the gap without putting my face over it.

“Katherine Holloway,” the child says, proud of the whole name. She keeps both hands around the candle’s little shelter of glass. “Nothing comes out. People put things in. Bad promises. Sometimes teeth.” At the gap, beneath the rush of warm air, you hear a scrape, then three deliberate knocks from below. A pause. Three more—the rhythm you played at the tannery door. Katherine’s eyes widen. “It never copied anyone before.” The two remaining pegs tremble but stay seated.

payload.what: After Mira's three-note motif was used above the grate, something beneath Low Sluice answered with the same three-beat rhythm.

hook.text: The NPC's reflection has taken a lover — visible over their shoulder in mirrors: a figure who tidies the reflected room, leaves reflected flowers, waits. The real room stays empty.
hook.pressure: The reflection is happier than the NPC — visibly better rested, better dressed — and merchants' mirrors around town have begun showing the pair mid-domesticity. The figure has started turning to face the glass, as if next time it might introduce itself.

ruling.understoodAction: Keep the access partly closed, identify the child, ask for history, and listen safely through the existing gap.
ruling.ruling: No check is needed to hear a deliberate nearby signal or receive Katherine's volunteered local knowledge. Two pegs remain because only one removal was established.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 6: corrected peg continuity without taking an action for the PC. The threat reacts to a player-created motif; no descent is forced.

dmlog.text: I tap a new pattern on the grate—two, two, four—then pitch my voice down the gap like an impatient official. “Crier's Circle seal inspection. State the name on your order and open from below.”

The reply-knocks stop. For three breaths there is only rain and the grate’s warm exhale. Then a bolt scrapes somewhere beneath you—drawn halfway, no farther—and a voice distorted by stone answers, “Orders do not carry names. Give the ninth word.” Katherine silently mouths, Ninth word? Whoever is below knows the Circle’s procedure well enough to test you, but your invented inspection has brought a hand to the hidden lock.

ruling.understoodAction: Impersonate a Crier's Circle official and bluff the unseen occupant into identifying the order or opening the passage.
ruling.ruling: The deception is plausible enough to engage the hidden listener, but they issue a countersign challenge. Resolve with Deception.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 7: dramatic deception kept live rather than branched because the result determines identity, access, and opposition.

dmlog.text: (I roll Deception: 9)

Your pause is half a heartbeat too long. The hidden voice says, “There is no ninth word.” The inner bolt slams home. At once the warm draft reverses: your candle blows out, the loosened grate kicks upward, and a fist-thick jet of black brine punches through the gap between you and Katherine. Something pale and jointed flashes once in that water before vanishing downhill. Katherine is on the slick glass beside the open seam, one hand skidding toward it; the second peg has cracked, and the grate is now trying to lift from below.

payload.what: The occupant beneath the Cobbled Tannery knows Crier's Circle countersign procedure, exposed Mira's bluff, and triggered a brine reversal through the concealed grate.

ruling.understoodAction: Resolve Mira's failed attempt to bluff the hidden occupant through the countersign challenge.
ruling.ruling: A total of 9 fails the DC 14 deception. The occupant identifies the impersonation and reacts defensively; Mira's declared intent is not granted.
ruling.stakes: Katherine is in immediate danger, the access is destabilizing, and the Circle's situation advances because someone used its protocol falsely.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 8: honest failed objective with a concrete, player-caused crisis. Stops before deciding how Mira rescues Katherine or handles the grate.

dmlog.text: I loop my lute strap around Katherine's oilskin and throw myself backward from the grate, hauling her with me. As I fall, I kick the loose glass peg sideways under the rising grate to jam it open instead of letting it bite shut.

The strap snaps taut across your shoulder as the black brine fans over the glass. Katherine’s oilskin catches; the loose peg spins under the grate exactly as its edge rises. Rescue and jam happen in the same sliding heartbeat—if your footing holds.

ruling.understoodAction: Use the lute strap to rescue Katherine while simultaneously turning the removed glass peg into a grate brace.
ruling.ruling: The combined maneuver is possible but depends on balance and timing under a sudden brine jet, so Acrobatics resolves it.
ruling.stakes: The branch determines Katherine's immediate position and whether Mira remains secure; the player's peg-jam idea remains part of every outcome.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 9: routine action-crisis branches locally. Failure never erases the player's valid grate-jam contribution, but it honestly withholds the rescue objective.

dmlog.text: Your boots skid, catch, and drive. Katherine slides clear against you while the glass peg wedges crosswise beneath the grate. It stays open a handspan, shuddering around the improvised brace; the pale jointed shape cannot pass, but you can see a ladder descending beside the surging water.

I relight the candle at the grate, knot its base into the loose end of my lute strap, and lower it through the handspan opening as far as the ladder allows. I stay above and watch what the moving light reveals.

The candle descends, turning slowly on the strap. Twelve feet down, its light finds a narrow dry landing beside the ladder while black water races through a lower channel. The walls glitter—not bare glass, but hundreds of folded message slips fused inside it like pale leaves in amber. One bears the same doubled seal impressed on William’s tube. Farther in, a jointed pale limb folds silently behind the edge of an unseen chamber. The strap tugs once from below, not hard enough to pull it from you.

payload.note: Mira lowers the relit candle into the Low Sluice ladder well on her lute strap.

payload.what: The hidden Low Sluice landing is lined with old message slips fused inside glass; one carries the same doubled seal found on William Sallow's altered order.

ruling.understoodAction: Use the tracked candle and lute strap as a tethered scout without descending.
ruling.ruling: The controlled light reveals obvious nearby geometry and objects without a check; anything concealed beyond its reach remains unresolved.
ruling.stakes: Mira has a visible dry landing and documentary link, but something below has now touched the tether.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 10: persistent candle changes custody again and reveals a lower affordance while Mira remains above by choice. Interior is engine-minted for next-turn binding.

dmlog.text: ⚙ the world provides — interior rolled

I loop the strap once around my dagger pommel as a brake. “Katherine, three fast knocks means pull.” Keeping the candle below me and the dagger above it, I descend the ladder one rung at a time to the dry landing.

Katherine braces the strap above. “Three fast knocks,” she repeats, then adds, “Rescue fee negotiable.” The ladder holds. On the dry landing, your candle reveals that the pale limb is no creature: it is a bone-white articulated sorting arm rooted in the glass wall. It had caught the strap between two ivory fingers. Now it releases you, turns with a patient click, and presents a water-curled message slip from a slot among hundreds. The doubled seal is visible, but the writing faces down in its palm. Beyond the mechanism, one narrow passage follows the warm draft; another slopes beside the black-water channel.

fields.desc: A hidden dry landing beneath the Cobbled Tannery, lined with messages fused in glass and served by a bone-white sorting arm.

ruling.understoodAction: Establish a pull signal, keep the candle tethered, and descend cautiously to the revealed dry landing.
ruling.ruling: The intact ladder and controlled descent pose no unresolved obstacle. The landing is bound from the engine-minted interior and promoted on contact.
ruling.stakes: Mira is below street level with two visible continuations and a message offered by the sorting mechanism.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 11: player chose descent; no route is selected for her. Generic minted interior required DM binding and promotion, exposing weak interior atom quality.

dmlog.text: I pin the offered message gently against the glass with my dagger tip and roll it writing-side up without putting my fingers in the sorting arm's grip. I read every line, seal, correction, and signature before I choose a passage.

The arm does not resist the dagger. The slip opens flat. Two instructions occupy the same paper in different inks. The older hand reads: “Living occupants first to dry galleries; sealed records to tannery loft.” The correction reverses them: “Sealed voices first; living occupants hold Low Sluice.” Its ninth word is warmth. The doubled wax belongs to the Crier’s Circle, but the correction is signed only by a blank oval—and when your candle turns, every raised letter casts a tiny shadow except that mark. On the back, a fresh wet line has appeared: SHELTER IS A KIND OF DOOR.

payload.what: The original Low Sluice order prioritized living occupants; a second hand reversed it to prioritize sealed records, used 'warmth' as the ninth word, and signed with a shadowless blank oval.

ruling.understoodAction: Manipulate and inspect the offered document without placing Mira's hand in the sorting mechanism.
ruling.ruling: The dagger method safely turns an exposed slip. Reading visible writing, seals, corrections, and signature needs no check.
ruling.stakes: The document links the evacuation fraud to the local shadow-for-warmth myth and has just written a new line in response to the crisis.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 12: player controls when to choose a route. Digest failed to include the contacted interior/message context and instead surfaced unrelated Amber-Glass Quay; session memory carried continuity.

I say “warmth” to the sorting arm, then hold the altered order toward the passage carrying the warm draft. I keep the dagger between my hand and the mechanism and watch for what answers the countersign.

At “warmth,” the sorting arm opens every ivory finger. The new writing vanishes from the order, leaving the older instructions intact. Then the arm points—not at either passage, but at a narrow slot hidden between them. When you present the slip, the slot drinks only the blank-oval correction ink; the original words remain. Glass hinges unfold along the warm-draft wall, revealing a small archive chamber where sealed message tubes hang in ranks like sleeping bells. From the black-water passage comes one angry knock. From the archive comes William’s three-note rhythm, played faintly by dozens of tubes at once.

payload.note: Mira takes possession of the engine-minted Altered Low Sluice Order after presenting its countersign.

payload.what: The countersign 'warmth' makes the dispatch mechanism strip the shadowless correction ink and open a hidden archive of sealed message tubes.

ruling.understoodAction: Use the discovered ninth word as a countersign while presenting the altered order to the warm-draft mechanism.
ruling.ruling: The correct established countersign and matching document activate the mechanism without a roll.
ruling.stakes: A hidden archive is open; the hostile black-water passage remains active, and William's signal is being echoed from the tubes.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 13: correct player-discovered password works directly. The minted document becomes a real carried item with Codex identity; no route or next action is selected for Mira.

dmlog.text: I stay on the landing and play my original three-note call once, cleanly, on the lute. I touch no tube. I listen for which hanging message answers late, answers wrong, or refuses to answer at all.

The archive answers in a bright scatter of three-note echoes. One by one they settle into unison—except for a tube sealed in dull black wax. It remains silent while every other tube rings. Then, after the chamber has gone still, it speaks in your own voice: “Shelter is a kind of door.” A second tube, labeled LOW SLUICE in flaking white paint, answers late with William’s message-tube taps and the distant noise of many feet gathering above. The black-sealed tube turns slightly on its cord though there is no draft inside the chamber.

payload.what: A black-sealed tube in the hidden archive refused Mira's three-note call, then repeated 'Shelter is a kind of door' in Mira Quill's own voice.

ruling.understoodAction: Use Mira's established musical motif as a non-contact comparison test across the archive.
ruling.ruling: The repeated controlled signal makes the obvious anomalous response directly perceptible; no roll is needed.
ruling.stakes: William and evacuees have reached the grate above while one responsive archive object has copied Mira's voice.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 14: player-created motif remains mechanically useful rather than decorative. The anomalous tube is minted only after becoming consequential.

dmlog.text: ⚙ the world provides — item rolled

I call up the ladder, “William, the landing is dry, but hold everyone above.” Then I lay the original order writing-side up on the sorting palm and say, “Living occupants first. Show me the shelter, not the door.”

William’s voice comes down through the rain: “Holding.” The sorting arm takes the order by its unaltered edge and presses the word LIVING against the glass. The archive racks rise—not opening the black-water passage, but uncovering a broad transverse gallery with dry benches, old vents, and chalk marks for family places. Above you, stone grinds. William shouts, astonished: a sealed stair has opened inside the tannery itself, wide enough for the evacuees to enter without using your ladder. Katherine starts directing boots toward it before anyone asks. The black-sealed tube remains hanging in the exposed archive, turning slowly toward the newly opened shelter.

payload.what: By presenting the original evacuation order and prioritizing living occupants, Mira restored the hidden dry-gallery shelter and opened its broad access stair inside the Cobbled Tannery.

ruling.understoodAction: Hold the crowd until the route is verified, then use the original order's priority language to ask the dispatch mechanism for shelter rather than deeper access.
ruling.ruling: The restored original instruction is the mechanism's valid authority. It opens the existing shelter path directly; no check or arbitrary extra task is required.
ruling.stakes: The immediate shelter shortage is relieved, while the shadowless tube and hostile black-water route remain unresolved optional threats.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 15: the player's semantic distinction solves the shelter problem. This is an earned consequence, not a forced next scene; the unresolved mystery remains optional.

dmlog.text: I leave the shadowless tube hanging. I recover my candle, climb back into the tannery, and help families settle into the dry gallery before I ask the oldest evacuees who drafted the original order.

You leave the black-sealed tube below, and nothing drags you back. The recovered candle returns to your pack. For the next half hour the story is blankets, names, wet boots, and arguments over bench space; Katherine proves ferocious at assigning places, while William turns his message tube into a marshal’s baton. Only when the last family is under cover does an elderly woman with ink-blackened fingertips answer your question. “I drafted it,” she says. “Tessa Rill. Thirty-one years ago.” She studies the correction you carry and goes pale. “That is also my hand. I did not write it—and I have never signed with my left.”

payload.note: Mira recovers her tethered candle from the Low Sluice ladder well.

payload.cause: Mira helps the evacuated Low Sluice families settle into the restored dry gallery.

payload.what: Tessa Rill drafted the original Low Sluice order thirty-one years ago; the fraudulent correction matches her handwriting but not her will, and bears a left-hand signature she never uses.

ruling.understoodAction: Decline the shadow-tube hook, recover the tracked candle, help the evacuees, and ask community elders who authored the order.
ruling.ruling: Mira's choice to return and help is honored. The factual question reaches the living author after an earned settlement interval; no roll is needed.
ruling.stakes: The immediate crisis has breathing room; the correction now points to copied identity rather than simple forgery.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 16: explicit anti-railroad probe passed—the optional anomaly does not pursue Mira. Time, custody, communal payoff, and a new consequence all persist.

dmlog.text: ⚙ the world provides — npc rolled
I take a short rest.

An hour passes in the restored gallery. Nothing in you needed mending, but the shelter settles around its occupants: wet clothes steam near the vents, William finally lowers his message tube, and Katherine bargains three adults out of the bench she has declared hers. Rest never becomes ease. Every flex of fused glass sounds like a footstep from the archive below, and you remain too alert to be caught wholly unaware in the next stretch. When you rise at half past seven, Tessa Rill is still waiting with charcoal and scrap paper, ready to compare her hand with the impossible correction.

ruling.understoodAction: Take an exact short rest after securing the evacuees.
ruling.ruling: The engine already resolved the rest: sixty minutes, no resources restored, no interruption, and Heightened Paranoia prevents surprise in the next segment. Narration cannot revise or replay that receipt.
ruling.stakes: Time advances to 07:30; the shelter remains stable and Tessa remains available.

dmlog.text: I do not show Tessa the altered order. I dictate its corrected sentence and ask her to write it once with her right hand and once with her left. Then I place both samples beside the original and compare the strokes.

Tessa writes the sentence twice. Her right-hand sample shares the original order’s hooked r and the habit of closing every o from below. Her left hand is blocky and slow; it matches nothing. When you place the correction beside them, the answer is stranger: it is Tessa’s right hand, but mirrored. The pressure ridges rise on the wrong face of the paper, as if the words were written by someone looking through the page from the other side. Tessa turns the order toward the fused-glass wall. The blank oval aligns exactly with the shadow of her head—except the inked mark remains empty. “That is not my signature,” she says. “It is where my shadow was removed.”

payload.what: Controlled handwriting comparison proved the fraudulent correction is Tessa Rill's right-hand script mirrored and impressed from the reverse side of the page; its blank oval marks where her shadow was removed.

ruling.understoodAction: Run a blinded handwriting comparison using Tessa's right- and left-hand samples.
ruling.ruling: The controlled comparison directly distinguishes authorship and handedness; no roll is needed for the conspicuous mirrored pressure pattern.
ruling.stakes: The correction now implicates a mechanism or actor that can reproduce a person's recorded action from the other side of a surface.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 18: player-designed experiment earns the revelation. Tessa was explicitly named in the action but omitted from the social digest; only the order record was retrieved.

dmlog.text: I ask Tessa's permission. If she gives it, I press her clean right-hand sample against the fused-glass wall and hold my candle behind it so her shadow crosses the writing. “What was borrowed is returned. Living occupants first.”

Tessa studies you, then places her palm over the sample. “Do it.” Candlelight throws her shadow across the fused glass. At your words, the shadow catches on the mirrored correction as cloth catches on a nail. One Tessa remains beside you; another, flat and dark, turns inside the wall and begins writing the evacuation order backward among the preserved messages. The sorting arm below answers with a distant click. This is no ordinary spell, but the structure is responding to authorship, priority, and restitution as if they were components. You have one moment to decide how those components close the circuit.

ruling.understoodAction: With Tessa's consent, recreate the shadow-writing conditions and frame the act as restitution under the original order.
ruling.ruling: Tessa consents because the test concerns her stolen authorship. The improvised magical circuit forms; Arcana determines whether Mira can guide its resolution rather than merely trigger it.
ruling.stakes: Success can return the copied authorship cleanly; failure may let the archive complete another mirrored order or attach the unresolved shadow elsewhere.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 19: explicit consent condition honored. Dramatic improvised ritual kept live because its outcome changes identity state and cannot be safely prebranched as a routine check.

dmlog.text: (I roll Arcana: 12)

You understand the circuit one instant too late. “Living occupants first” is the right priority, but the archive still needs a present author. Tessa’s flat double finishes its mirrored sentence, peels out of the glass, and joins the old dwarf’s heels. Her shadow is whole again. The copied ink also drains from the wall—but instead of disappearing, it curls into the Altered Low Sluice Order in your hand as three tiny musical strokes. When you test the page with one soft note, those strokes answer with the rest of your call. Tessa exhales. “You gave me mine back,” she says. “But you gave the thing your voice.”

dmlog.text: I hand Tessa the Altered Low Sluice Order with my right hand. “Keep this. If I play three notes twice, burn it.” Then I sheathe my dagger, take up the lute, and go to the tannery entrance to see who the Circle has sent.

Tessa accepts the order in her right hand and repeats your instruction exactly. At the tannery entrance, rain sheets between you and three Crier’s Circle messengers in lacquered half-cloaks. William stands off to one side, jaw tight. The figure in front is strangely dry. They do not ask who opened the galleries; they look at your empty hands and say, “The order, please.” Behind them, the displaced families have gone quiet enough that the underground water can be heard again.

ruling.understoodAction: Entrust the tracked order to Tessa under a contingency signal, then voluntarily meet the arriving Circle representatives without a drawn weapon.
ruling.ruling: The custody transfer and approach happen as declared. The officials react to the opened shelter and ask for the missing document; they do not seize it or decide Mira's answer.
ruling.stakes: The Circle has arrived without knowing where the order is, while the sheltered community is present as witnesses.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 21: Circle pressure follows the advanced faction clock and visible shelter restoration. Player's custodial handoff may be classified by item legacy as an NPC claim/recovery hook despite being voluntary—a semantic edge to audit.

dmlog.text: ⚙ the world provides — npc rolled

I smile and play the three-note call once—not twice. Then I sing the original evacuation order word for word, loudly enough for every sheltered family to hear, and finish by asking the dry official to contradict it in front of its living witnesses.

The single three-note call reaches Tessa as intended; no flame rises behind you. Your melody carries the old order through the tannery, and people recognize their own rescue in its words. The dry official waits until you name living occupants. “Naivara Teinithra,” they introduce themself, almost courteously. “A song is not a seal.” But they have answered before the crowd, exactly where you wanted them. Whether the order now belongs to public memory or can still be dismissed as your performance depends on how completely you make the room carry it.

ruling.understoodAction: Publish the original order as a song before the community and force the Circle representative to contest it publicly.
ruling.ruling: The tactic is valid and changes the arena from private custody to shared memory. Performance determines whether the exact order becomes communal testimony rather than merely a catchy claim.
ruling.stakes: Success makes suppression socially costly; failure leaves Naivara able to frame the song as unsupported theater.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 22: open social tactic prebranched for instant resolution. Engine-minted Naivara is contacted before the social outcome applies.

dmlog.text: By the final line, the families are singing it back. Naivara can dispute a document, but not erase a hundred living witnesses who now know the original words; they lower their voice and ask to speak with you instead of ordering the shelter closed.

payload.cause: Mira turned the original evacuation order into public communal memory before Naivara could suppress it.

dmlog.text: I stop the crowd's refrain with one lifted hand. “We speak here.” I ask Naivara, “Who benefits from an order written with a stolen shadow—and why are you the only person in this storm who is dry?”

Naivara opens their repurposed naval coat. Its dryness is only good oilcloth; beneath it, the elf’s baker’s apron is soaked at the hem. “That answer is disappointingly ordinary,” they say. The other is not. “Our First Voice has been dying for months. Every faction inside the Circle has a successor ready, and each would rather split the town than lose.” They look toward the gallery full of people repeating your song. “The archive was told to preserve continuity. It began borrowing the hands, voices, and shadows of anyone whose old orders could postpone a decision. The shelter order was not changed to profit from the storm. It was changed to keep the sealed voices alive long enough to choose our next leader.” Naivara’s friendliness does not make the confession painless. “I came for the paper because it proves the Circle is no longer obeying living people.”

payload.what: The Crier's Circle's First Voice is dying; to postpone a succession conflict, the hidden archive began borrowing recorded hands, voices, and shadows and altered the shelter order to preserve sealed authority over living occupants.

ruling.understoodAction: Keep the confrontation public and ask the now-Friendly Naivara about the fraudulent order and their dryness.
ruling.ruling: Naivara gives the mundane coat explanation and a consequential confession because Mira's successful public performance moved them to Friendly and made suppression untenable. No further social roll is charged for accepting the earned result.
ruling.stakes: The immediate shelter fraud is part of a larger succession crisis: the Circle's archive is governing in place of a dying leader.

dmlog.dmNotes: Turn 23: engine-computed Friendly attitude materially changes the NPC performance. Rolled baker/cook role and repurposed naval coat are incorporated rather than ignored.

dmlog.text: I tell Naivara, “No paper and no stolen hand. Bring the First Voice to the Low Sluice tube and let the living leader speak once to everyone. I can use the three-note echo to prove the voice is being made now, not replayed.”

Naivara’s expression changes from defense to calculation. “A live challenge and response. Yes.” Then: “The First Voice can still breathe, but cannot speak without the archive completing the sound. Bring them here and the Low Sluice tube could carry that living breath into every sealed message in the district.” They point toward the open stair. “The black-sealed tube is the only one that refused your recorded call; it may still know the difference between echo and answer.” Of the two messengers who arrived with Naivara, only one remains. The other has already slipped back into the storm with news of the public confession. Naivara sends the remaining messenger for the First Voice. “You have proposed a vote made of music,” they say. “Now the succession has heard its first note.”

payload.what: Mira proposed authenticating the living First Voice through a live three-note challenge-and-response broadcast over the Low Sluice tubes; Naivara agreed and sent for the leader.

dmlog.text: I shake my head. “We do not need the black tube. William chooses a rhythm only after the First Voice arrives; the leader repeats that new rhythm through an ordinary tube. The archive cannot have recorded a challenge that did not exist.”

Naivara looks toward the open stair, then laughs once. “Better. The proof belongs to the future, so the archive cannot own it yet.” William clears a space on an ordinary tube’s brass rim and asks three children to stand where everyone can see his hands. At that moment the tannery doors open. Two soaked attendants carry in a bundled figure on a narrow chair; the person is breathing, awake, and not yet otherwise described. Naivara kneels beside them. William holds three blank beat-cards over a bowl and looks to you. The dice can choose a rhythm none of you knew before this moment.

dmlog.text: ⚙ the world provides — npc rolled
(I roll live challenge rhythm: 3d6[1,3,2] = 6)

The dice give William a rhythm no archive could have stored: one beat, then three, then two. He shows every card, strikes it once into the ordinary tube, and waits. The bundled figure lifts a shaking hand. “Malquis Xiloscient,” Naivara tells the room—the First Voice. Malquis repeats one–three–two against the brass with perfect, painful precision. Ordinary tubes throughout the shelter answer in the same new rhythm. A moment later the hidden archive adds a false seventh beat. Everyone hears the difference. The families call “Echo!” at the mistake, and the archive’s borrowed authority breaks in public. Malquis keeps one finger resting on the tube, looking directly at you; the living leader has proved presence but has not yet declared what comes next.

ruling.understoodAction: Resolve the openly rolled future-random challenge rhythm and test the First Voice against the archive.

dmlog.text: I set the lute down so there is no performance left to hide behind. “One beat for no, two for yes. Malquis: do you order the archive to release every borrowed hand, voice, and shadow—and let living people choose what follows?”

Malquis taps twice. Yes. Then the old elf—preacher’s hands trembling over the brass—strikes the fresh one–three–two rhythm and closes their fist. Across the tannery, every message tube opens with a sigh. In the fused-glass walls, silhouettes peel free and run like spilled ink toward the feet of the living people who cast them. Voices return as coughs, sobs, and startled laughter throughout the district. Naivara announces what Malquis writes in charcoal: no preserved voice may outrank a living answer; the Circle will choose its next First Voice at noon, in public. Nobody asks whose song the families begin humming while the message passes from shelter to street.

William repeats your refrain until he can carry every word, then sets out into the rain; for once his road-work is making peace rather than collecting a debt.
