I accept the tube with my right hand. I tap the fresh one–three–two rhythm into it and say, “No preserved voice outranks a living answer.” Then I hold it to my ear and wait to hear who answers first.

The new tube takes the one–three–two rhythm without echoing it back. For several seconds there is only rain on the tannery roof. Then a living voice answers from very far away, breathless and young: “I heard you. The stone hives by the old wheel are singing your shelter song. The bees came back this morning, but they are made of glass.” The connection closes with the creak of a vast turning wheel. Around you, the Living-First Song continues without needing the tube at all. The instrument in your hand has remembered only the answer, not your command.

Tessa turns the tube beneath the gray window and listens without touching its seal. “I cannot tell.” An archive echo and a living reply can share the same cadence. Only a contradiction would separate them: ask something never entered into any record. If it answers, it lives—or something is listening now. If it only repeats, it is residue. She sets it down. “But asking may teach it the question.”

The tube did not retrieve a fact; it supplied the answer the test expected to have. Somewhere inside the glass, a second click follows—late, soft, and not part of the reply.

dmlog.text: I ask Naivara for directions to the old creaking wheel, but I make no promise to go. I want to know who controls the road and what the glass-bee report cost its sender.

Naivara traces the route in spilled flour: east along the raised salt road, then north where the leat crosses beneath it. The old wheel is roughly two hours away. No one truly controls that road now; the Circle abandoned its tollhouse, though someone still rings its bell after dark. Of the glass-bee sender, she knows only the price that arrived: the return tube was clean, and no courier came home with it. She leaves the choice of going entirely yours.

dmlog.text: I stay away from the ringing bell. I scrape rain-black grit from the oldest law plaque and compare its original exemption marks with the fresh signs above it, looking for who is still legally allowed through this quarter.

The grit gives way to three older exemptions: water carriers, burial carts, and apothecaries bearing sealed vials. The fresh board preserves only Circle officers. Beneath a tampered floorboard you find a merchant ledger listing glass-vial deliveries to the tollhouse after it was supposedly abandoned. No bell rings while you read. The lawful route forward is a narrow passage roofed in loose gravel; crossing quietly would keep whoever changed the sign from knowing you found their supply trail.

payload.what: The abandoned tollhouse continued receiving sealed glass-vial shipments after closure, under an erased apothecary exemption.

dmlog.text: I cut two strips from the edge of my bedroll, wrap them over my boots, and cross the loose-gravel passage slowly. I keep one hand on the wall and stop whenever the toll bell moves.

The bedroll cloth deadens your first step, but the roof is laid to betray weight, not footwear: gravel shifts under the boards and clicks against a glass channel hidden in the wall. Your slow pace gives you a chance to cross between its pulses. A clean passage would reach the guard post unseen; a loud one will ring the toll bell for whoever waits beyond. Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check, DC 13—the improvised wraps have lowered the usual difficulty.

ruling.understoodAction: Muffle the loose-gravel alarm with strips cut from the bedroll and cross cautiously.
ruling.ruling: The idea helps but cannot bypass a pressure channel built under the whole passage; it lowers the Stealth DC from 15 to 13.
ruling.stakes: Success reaches the next section unseen; failure rings the toll bell and gives the guards the initiative.

dmlog.text: (I roll Stealth: 18)

The cloth catches each sliding pebble before it reaches the glass channel. You cross unheard and reach the burned guard post above the next street. Below, a sinkhole has opened through the boulevard. Two Circle guards in old plague masks wait on opposite sides, watching the obvious approaches but not your ledge. Between them, a mud-sled bears fresh crates stamped with the erased apothecary exemption.

ruling.understoodAction: Resolve the muffled crossing with Stealth 18 against DC 13.
ruling.ruling: Success; the alarm remains silent and Mira reaches the next segment unseen.
ruling.stakes: Resolved

dmlog.text: Still hidden, I use Minor Illusion to ring the toll bell from the far roof. When the guards turn, I cut the mud-sled’s brake rope and try to send its loaded crates sliding into the sinkhole between them.

Your false bell turns both masks toward the far roof. The cut rope snaps, but the loaded sled hesitates on one warped runner; gravity needs a precise kick before the guards look back. Time it well and the crates will divide them at the sinkhole. Miss, and the sled will clang broadside while both still share a clear route to you. Make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, DC 12.

ruling.understoodAction: Use Minor Illusion as a diversion, release the loaded mud-sled, and split the guards with the sinkhole.
ruling.ruling: The illusion works; placing the unstable sled requires precise timing.
ruling.stakes: Success separates the guards before combat; failure alerts both with an open route to Mira.

dmlog.text: (I roll Sleight of Hand: 10)

Your kick lands too high. The sled turns broadside and slams the curb; every crate answers with a glass chorus. Both masks snap toward you. One guard vaults the sinkhole while the other draws a spear behind the stalled cargo, leaving you on the ledge with retreat open but the shipment between them. The bell begins ringing by itself. Their surprise is gone; yours is not yet a surrender.

ruling.understoodAction: Resolve Sleight of Hand 10 against DC 12.
ruling.ruling: Failure; the sled stalls loudly and both guards engage.
ruling.stakes: Resolved

dmlog.text: I drop behind the stalled crates and do not attack. I shout, “The old law protects apothecaries, not kidnappers. Tell me who signed these shipments.” I keep the crates between us and focus entirely on dodging their spears.

You fold behind the cargo and make the law your shield as carefully as the crates. The nearer guard answers, “No signature. The hives choose what leaves.” The other says nothing; both advance with spears, unwilling to discuss who the vials are for. Your refusal to strike gives them one last chance to stop, but it also leaves the next proof to their choices. You watch their shoulders and give ground only when steel commits.

effect.note: attacks against them have disadvantage until their next turn; Dex saves at advantage

ruling.understoodAction: Take the Dodge action behind cover while demanding the shipment’s authority.
ruling.ruling: The guards disclose one clue but continue the attack; the engine resolves both spear actions against Dodge.
ruling.stakes: The guards may wound Mira; their refusal identifies the hives as the source of authority.

dmlog.text: Their answer is enough for now. I keep talking so their eyes stay on my face, then break for the roof ledge without giving either spear an opening. I am not trying to win this fight; I am taking the truth about the hives back to Tessa.

You let the nearer spear commit to the crate, then slip the other way. The roof ledge is barely a path—wet slate, a gutter, one blind drop—but the guards will not follow beyond the tollhouse bell. Behind you, one calls, ‘Bring that answer back and the hives will know your name.’ The stalled shipment remains theirs. The erased law and their confession remain yours.

payload.reason: Mira withdraws along the roof ledge with the evidence

effect.note: no opportunity attacks on this turn's move

ruling.understoodAction: Disengage from the guards and leave by the roof ledge with the discovered evidence.
ruling.ruling: The legal exit is reachable without a check after Disengage; the guards do not pursue beyond their post.
ruling.stakes: Mira escapes unharmed but leaves the shipment in hostile custody.

dmlog.text: I stay above the street and follow the oldest plaques away from the tollhouse. At the next open courtyard I stop long enough to copy every surviving office name, seal, and amendment that mentions the stone hives or the apothecary exemption.

The roofline empties into a mud-choked courtyard where three generations of law survive on the same wall. Beneath soot and a newer quarantine seal, you find the original charter: the stone hives were municipal dispensaries, and their keeper answered to the Office of Amber Weights. Someone has chiseled away the officeholder’s name—but not the seal shaped like a split honeycomb.

payload.what: The stone hives were founded as municipal dispensaries under the Office of Amber Weights, whose seal is a split honeycomb.

ruling.understoodAction: Advance along the roof route and study the surviving civic plaques.
ruling.ruling: The carved history is freely readable and yields a named office and seal.
ruling.stakes: The guards retain the shipment, but Mira gains a traceable authority above them.

dmlog.text: Before I move on, I read my notes back to myself. What exactly have I established about the Office of Amber Weights, the split-honeycomb seal, and its relationship to the stone hives?

Three things are certain. The hives were built as public dispensaries, not private storehouses. Their lawful chain ran through the Office of Amber Weights. That office used the split-honeycomb seal. The guards’ claim that ‘the hives choose’ replaces a named civic authority with superstition—or conceals whoever inherited that authority after the office vanished.

ruling.understoodAction: Recite only the facts already established about the hives and their former authority.
ruling.ruling: No new fact is invented; the answer distinguishes canon from inference.
ruling.stakes: None; this is a continuity check.

dmlog.text: I continue toward the boarding-house hub, keeping the courtyard wall between me and the tollhouse. I listen for the strangers humming that same unfamiliar tune, and I watch their hands as closely as their faces.

The courtyard wall carries you beyond the tollhouse into a torchlit boarding-house square. A street performer worries three bright notes from a wire-strung bow—the same tune—while sleepers watch from the windows. Their smile follows your face; their free hand follows your pouch. The crowd closes and opens around them like practiced scenery. Make a Wisdom (Insight) check, DC 14, to catch the theft before the hand withdraws.

ruling.understoodAction: Reach the boarding-house hub under cover, listen for the shared tune, and scrutinize the strangers for concealed intent.
ruling.ruling: The wall keeps Mira out of the tollhouse guards’ immediate sight. Her close attention engages the hub’s pickpocket problem as an Insight check.
ruling.stakes: Success catches the performer in the act; a near miss prevents the theft but loses control of them; failure lets them slip inside after touching Mira’s pouch.

dmlog.text: The performer bows, the crowd parts, and only then do you feel the tug at your pouch. They vanish through the boarding-house door before you can tell what their fingers found. The three-note tune continues from somewhere upstairs.

I stop in the boarding-house doorway and check my pouch without taking my eyes off the stairs. Then I ask the desk keeper which room the performer ran toward, and whether anyone inside has been humming that same three-note tune.

No coin is gone, and nothing obvious is missing. Something has been added: a scorched cloth room-tag marked O.A.W.—7 beneath your candles. The desk keeper sees it and stops pretending to polish the register. ‘Seven. Nobody has checked out of Seven, but nobody sleeps there. The rent arrives every new moon.’ Upstairs, the three-note tune cuts off mid-phrase. The performer has given you a room and a warning.

payload.what: Room Seven of the dream-touched boarding house remains paid through each new moon although nobody sleeps there; its room tags bear the initials O.A.W.

ruling.understoodAction: Check the pouch after the failed pickpocket read, hold the doorway, and question the desk keeper about the performer and the shared tune.
ruling.ruling: The authoritative purse and carried inventory show no confirmed loss among the surfaced contents. The segment’s scorched cloth tag and the retrieved occupied-room record combine into a planted clue; the keeper answers without a check because Mira presents direct evidence.

dmlog.text: I do not take the bait and follow the performer upstairs. I tie the scorched room-tag to the alley belfry, play the three-note tune back deliberately wrong on my lute, and watch the square to see who corrects me or moves toward Room Seven.

You knot the scorched tag beneath the belfry clapper and give the square its tune with the last note bent deliberately flat. Heads turn. Two sleepers lean from separate windows; the desk keeper freezes; somewhere above, a floorboard answers. The trick is not making them hear you—it is making the true listener reveal that the mistake matters. Make a Charisma (Performance) check, DC 12.

payload.note: Mira ties the scorched O.A.W.—7 room tag beneath the alley belfry clapper as bait.

ruling.understoodAction: Reject the obvious pursuit, place the room tag on the alley belfry, and use an intentionally flawed performance as a public counter-trap.
ruling.ruling: The alternate approach is valid and does not advance Mira into Room Seven. Placing the tag is deterministic; isolating a meaningful reaction from the crowd requires Performance.
ruling.stakes: Success identifies a response from the supposedly empty room; a near miss reveals only collective orientation; failure makes noise without isolating the tune’s source.

dmlog.text: You repeat the flattened note. The square winces, but Room Seven answers with the correct pitch—once, sharply—from behind its closed shutter. A second figure across the square starts toward the boarding house, realizes you saw them, and turns away.

payload.what: When Mira deliberately played the shared tune wrong, the supposedly empty Room Seven answered with the correct final note.

dmlog.text: Where is the Scorched Cloth Room Tag now?
Scorched Cloth Room Tag is held by the alley belfry (place).

I leave the tag where it is and shadow the second figure away from the boarding house, keeping them between me and the lanterns. I want to learn whom they report to, not catch them or force a confrontation.

The figure leaves Room Seven behind and slips into an oval plaza glowing without lamps. At its edge, paving stones imitate a crosswalk a little too perfectly; beyond them, darkness is eating chips from a wall without leaving rubble. Two guard captains hold opposite balconies, watching for a report. You can trail your quarry through the wheelbarrow shadows before the pair closes its net. Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check, DC 13.

ruling.understoodAction: Reject Room Seven, shadow the responding figure away from the boarding house, and learn whom they report to without initiating a confrontation.
ruling.ruling: The player-directed detour is honored. The immediate generated exit is a void-struck plaza watched by an elite guard pair; the described lantern discipline permits a Stealth check before contact rather than forcing the encounter.
ruling.stakes: Success overhears the report unseen; a near miss enters the plaza with the guards searching; failure triggers the telegraphed elite-pair encounter while both listed escapes remain available.

dmlog.text: You become the courier’s shadow beneath the balcony. Their report names the tune as a command key: Room Seven woke, and the guards were ordered to feed more voices into the widening absence. Captain Ilyra Venn goes still. She takes the missing chain-link from the courier, jams it across the humming mechanism, and the void folds shut like a black eye. Its answering pressure vanishes across the district. The other captain runs. Venn removes her badge and says, to nobody she can see, ‘I will put every order in the public book.’ You entered unseen, heard the truth, and watched one enforcer break the machine and herself from its service.

dmlog.text: I step out where Captain Ilyra Venn can see me. I tell her I heard everything. I will carry copies of the orders to the public book, but I will not promise to protect her from what follows. I ask her to give me the evidence and tell me whether breaking the void also freed the strangers from the tune.

Venn does not ask twice for safety. She divides the orders into three oilskin packets and gives you one. ‘Copies are protection enough.’ The pages name collection sites, payments, and the instruction to use the three-note key on occupied rooms. Breaking the mechanism ended its pull; strangers may remember the tune, she says, but it can no longer steer them or feed the void. She keeps one packet and sends the courier with the third.

ruling.ruling: Venn’s established permanent defection and public-record goal make another persuasion roll unnecessary. She accepts distributed copies as safer than a single protected witness, transfers one mechanically tracked packet, and answers from the now-resolved segment state.

dmlog.text: (the player waits)

You wait. Venn watches the courier vanish into the alleys, then tears the badge from her coat and grinds its pin under her heel. Five minutes later the hammering east of the plaza changes rhythm: not a workshop now, but shutters being barred ahead of an approaching crowd. The water pump in the next square squeals once under no visible hand. Venn points west toward a dry loft above the closed weigh-house. ‘Rest there if you mean to. The street will not stay quiet.’

ruling.understoodAction: Mira waits to see what follows Venn’s choice.
ruling.ruling: Time advances and the next district pressure becomes audible; no player movement is forced.
ruling.stakes: The public evidence is moving, but a crowd is approaching.

dmlog.text: I take a short rest in the dry loft Venn pointed out.

The loft is real, dry, and barely large enough for your bedroll. Venn takes the stair while you bar the hatch with a broken scale beam. Below, the crowd noise passes in uneven waves. You put the lute under one hand, the copied orders under the other, and let the district spend an hour without you.

dmlog.text: I wake, check the light, and use the rooftops to return to the Office of Amber Weights rather than cross the crowd square.

The light is wrong. Your hour became four while the district moved beneath you: the crowd has passed east, leaving broken shutters and wet footprints around the pump. You take Venn’s westward roofline instead. The office returns below you—amber windows dark now, its scales chained—but the belfry tag still hangs across the square. Nothing forces you toward Room Seven or the crowd’s wake.

dmlog.text: I do not return to Room Seven. I use my dagger to open the Office of Amber Weights public notice cage and pin my entire packet of Venn’s orders inside, keeping no secret copy.

The notice cage is built to preserve official lies: amber glass, iron lattice, and a warded hasp carrying the same three-click office rhythm. Your dagger can lift the spring without shattering the pane, but only if you work between the belfry’s swings. If it catches, the office bell will wake the night clerk and whoever now owns the guard seal. Make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, DC 14.

ruling.understoodAction: Mira tries to publish her only packet without preserving private leverage.
ruling.ruling: The publication succeeds on success or near miss; failure leaves the packet with Mira but alerts the dominant faction.
ruling.stakes: Public evidence versus an alerted office network.

dmlog.text: The spring snaps back and the office bell rings twice. A lamp blooms behind the amber windows; boots strike the stair. The packet is still in your hand, but the office network now knows someone tried to breach its public cage.

I do not try the cage again. I climb the alley belfry, tie the opened packet of orders to its clapper beside the scorched tag, and ring until the pages and names are visible from every window. Then I take the roof toward segment four before the office boots reach the street.

You abandon the hasp and take the louder truth. The packet opens across the belfry clapper; each peal snaps names and payment columns into the torchlight. Windows rise before the office door opens. You are already crossing the west roof when the next courtyard flares orange—a warehouse top floor burning above trapped stables. Behind you, the orders keep ringing without you.

dmlog.text: I leave the office boots behind. I soak one of my costumes at the courtyard trough, wrap it over my face, lash its other half to the hitching post as a guide, and go into the burning stable calling for anyone trapped inside.

The wet cloth buys you one clean breath. Inside, smoke has erased the rafters and the stable partitions are beginning to lean. A groom answers from behind the far stall; a second voice is lower, beneath a fallen gate. Your costume guide keeps the courtyard visible, but reaching both before the roof drops will test how long you can stay conscious. Make a Constitution save, DC 12, with advantage from your preparation.

ruling.understoodAction: Mira uses a carried costume and the hitching post to make a smoke guide, then attempts a two-person rescue.
ruling.ruling: The preparation grants advantage; the save determines rescue completeness and smoke harm.
ruling.stakes: Two trapped people, Mira’s HP, and whether the burning segment is resolved.

dmlog.text: Smoke closes your throat before you reach the far stall. You crawl back by the wet cloth as the gate and roof collapse together. The voices vanish under timber; you reach the courtyard burned and coughing, with the rescue failed but your retreat still open.

dmlog.text: I do not go back under the collapsed roof. I mark the trapped stall from outside, hammer the fire-call on the hitching post, and return to the belfry square to bring a real rescue line rather than chase the sounds toward the dam.

You do not turn failure into another body. From the courtyard you score the trapped stall’s position into the hitching post and beat the district fire-call on its iron ring. Bucket runners answer from two streets. You lead them only to the safe edge, tell them exactly where the roof fell, then take the muddy west passage back. The belfry is still ringing; the office can no longer pretend nobody saw.

dmlog.text: Who is holding Copies of Venn’s Void Orders right now?
Copies of Venn’s Void Orders is held by the alley belfry (place).
I inspect the copies on the belfry from below, then ask the gathered witnesses who is willing to carry one named order to the public book while I keep moving.

The oilskins still hold, but soot has begun to blur the lowest signatures. A salt porter in a red scarf copies one complete order onto a flour wrapper, including the paymaster’s name, then reads it back beneath the belfry. Three witnesses correct the date together. She folds the wrapper under her coat and takes the lit arcade toward the public book. The originals remain overhead; their first independent copy has left by another road.

payload.what: A red-scarfed salt porter made a witnessed independent copy of one named void order and carried it toward the public book; Mira’s published originals remained on the alley belfry.

dmlog.text: I leave the belfry witnesses to their work, cross the sealed void plaza by the wheelbarrow route I used before, and continue to the far alley without seeking Venn or Room Seven.

The belfry keeps speaking after you leave it. You cross the oval plaza under Venn’s abandoned balcony, using the overturned wheelbarrow to avoid the mimic paving. The mechanism’s housing is split and silent; the darkness it fed has become an ordinary gap in the wall. No captain closes the route. At the far alley, fresh cart ruts descend toward water, while a narrower stair climbs above the roofs.
I take the descending cart ruts toward the water. Before committing to the next square, I stop behind cover and study its exits, occupants, and anything in reach that could become an escape route.

The cart ruts end above a square choked with people and runoff. A rumor is moving faster than the bodies: each retelling points the surge toward the belfry. Broken cobbles leave a narrow outer curb, but the middle has become black mud deep enough to catch a boot. The water pump stands above it, handle jerking as shoulders strike its basin. The roof stair remains behind you; a drainage arch opens beyond the crowd.

I take one costume from my pack, knot it high on the water pump as a false rally flag, and use my lute to repeat the crowd’s shouted phrase from the drainage arch. I want the surge to bend toward the flag while I take the outer curb.

You knot one costume above the pump where every shoulder can see it, then send the crowd’s own phrase back from the drainage arch in the voice of a street refrain. Heads turn before bodies do. The surge begins to shear around the basin, opening a wet outer line—but if your echo sounds like mockery instead of agreement, the same motion will point straight at you. Make a Charisma (Performance) check, DC 14.

payload.note: Mira knots one costume high on the water pump as a false rally flag while crossing the mob square.

dmlog.text: The echoed phrase lands as ridicule. Faces turn from the pump to you, and the outer curb disappears under a sideways shove. You hit the broken stones hard and crawl back to the cart-rut mouth before the surge closes, bruised, seen, and still on the near side of the drainage arch.

I do not shout over them again and I leave the costume on the pump. I drop below the curb, keep my lute under my coat, and crawl with the runoff toward the drainage arch while every face is still turned toward the belfry.

You let the crowd spend its anger uphill. In the gutter, their knees and elbows hide you better than any spell; runoff carries ash past your hands toward the arch. The danger is the final six feet, where the drain narrows beside the pump basin and anyone looking down will see your lute’s polished rim. Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check, DC 13. The cart-rut retreat remains behind you.
(I roll Stealth: 23)

You move when the crowd inhales. No boot touches you; no face turns. Beneath the arch, you find the dry maintenance lip hidden above the runoff and cross without wetting the lute. From there you can watch the flooded dead-end hall without entering it: pale figures wade against the current, following a candle stub that burns under water. A roof stair remains behind you. The hall waits for your decision.
